GUPTA DAIRY

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The State can now get back the money the Free State government paid the Guptas for the verde Dairy Project

Unique Selling Point:
Carte Blanche was the first media to visit the Vrede Dairy farm in 2014, and exposed the abysmal state of the animals and the lequipment which had been funded to the tune half a billion rand. . Last week the Free State High Court ordered that an amount not exceeding R220,202,652 “which constitutes proceeds of crime” could be seized by the AFU from various bank accounts linked to the Estina dairy project in Vrede in the Free State.

The vast sum of money was paid in seven tranches between April 2013 and May 2016. Soon after it had been deposited into the dairy project’s accounts, the money was transferred to the accounts of several other Gupta-linked companies.

Summary:
Is this the beginning of the end for the Zupta cabal? For the first time the NPA will be taking decisive action against the controversial Gupta family and their corruption. It was money destined for the Vrede Dairy that paid for the 2013 Gupta wedding at Sun City, while the herd of cows starved, and farm workers were paid subsistence wages.

Press Release:


Estina – Dairy Farm
In 2014, Carte Blanche investigated how a massive agricultural project, the Estina Diary Farm, which was meant to benefit local Free State farmers, became just another scheme for the Gupta family to milk the state of millions of tax-payers’ funds. Now, as the National Prosecuting Authority hones in on one of the biggest money laundering schemes, the dairy farm has once again taken centre stage in ongoing investigations into the State Capture project.


Script:


GUPTA DAIRY FARM

V/O: In 2014 Carte Blanche exposed the Vrede Dairy Farm Project in the Free State. We showed how the provincial government had gifted 4400 hectares of farm land, on a free 99-year lease, to a company with no farming experience. The Director of Estina, Kamal Wasram, was an IT salesman who had worked for the Gupta-owned company, Sahara Computers.

No tender process was followed, instead a Project Proposal was pushed through by MEC of Agriculture at the time, Mosebenzi Zwane, and allegedly signed off in Premier Ace Magashule’s office. With provincial funding of R342 million, it promised 600 jobs, and a livelihood for 100 emerging farmers.

But the dairy herd were diseased and dying. We found old bones, and skinny, underfed cows. The locals were still unemployed, and unpasteurized milk was being sold ….off the back of a bakkie, in plastic Coke bottles.

The Gupta’s lawyer at the time, Pieter van der Merwe, denied the family had any involvement with the Project, calling our suspicions “baseless and malicious.” However, he did confirm that Estina had used the consultancy services of Gupta associate company Linkway Projects.

Link: When Carte Blanche visited the Vrede Dairy farm 4 years ago, we showed the involvement of the Gupta family. We could see that very little of the Free State’s money was being spent on actual farming, but now court papers confirm that over R220 million ended up here, with the Guptas.

V/O: On the 18th of January the Asset Forfeiture Unit was granted a Preservation Order by the Bloemfontein High Court. It enables them to seize the dairy farm itself, and R220 million rand from individuals and companies who received dairy farm money. This includes R10 million paid to Atul Gupta himself.

Pauli: They didn’t want just the crumbs, they wanted the whole cake. From the AFU documents we now know that only R2 million from R220 million meant for empowering poor farmers, or emerging farmers, only R2 million actually went to the farm.

V/O: Pauli van Wyk is an investigative journalist with Scorpio, one of the teams sifting through the mountain of information in the Gupta Leaks.

Pauli: The money would go from the Free State Department of Agriculture to this Estina But from the Gupta Leaks and from the Financials we could see the money went from Estina towards companies outside of South Africa and right back in towards the wedding in the end, and to Oakbay.

V/O: The CEO of Oakbay is Ronica Ragavan. She is also a Director of Linkway Projects, which paid for the 2013 Gupta wedding. The lavish nuptials at Sun City enraged South Africans, because a civilian plane full of wedding guests was allowed to land at Waterkloof Airforce Base. At the time the country didn’t realise that the obscenely opulent celebrations, costing R30 million, had been funded by the Vrede Dairy Farm project.

Glynnis: Three months after the wedding Linkway sends an account to a place called Accurate Investments, a Gupta controlled shelf company in the UAE, and then you see the money flow from Estina. And it's for the V&A function at Sun City. That's the title of it, so you don't need to be a genius to join the dots. It includes things like – which I mean is really obscene – R13,000 for chocolate truffles, R2.3m for scarves, R13m for events services. That's your money, my money that's being used for this.

V/O: Former prosecutor Glynnis Breytenbach is now the DA’s shadow Minister for Justice. The party laid criminal charges against the Guptas and their cronies in July last year.

Glynnis: The main charge is money laundering and then there are one or two sub charges to that but in terms of the Prevention of Organized Crime Act, and all of that legislation.

V/O; One only has to follow the money to understand how brazen the looting was. R19 million was spent on a fleet of luxury cars through Stanlib.

Link: This drab industrial street in Boksburg is where another R15 million from the dairy farm ended up. VR Laser Services is a Gupta owned company that was doing business with arms manufacturer Denel – nothing to do with empowering emerging farmers or the community of Vrede.

V/O: The CEO of VR Laser Services is Pieter van der Merwe, the same Pieter van der Merwe who acted as the Gupta’s lawyer back in 2014, and denied they had any involvement in the Dairy project.

He explained in writing that VR Laser Services has done no work whatsoever for Estina. Also, that VR Laser Services and VR Laser Services Investments, are two completely different companies, with different shareholders and different directors.

But R15 million from Estina went to Gupta-man Salim Essa, who bought shares in the steel cutting business from VR Laser Services Investments.

Devi: Does this look like a Free State dairy farm to you? Of course, not – it’s the centre of Johannesburg where the diamond cutters and dealers are located. Oddly R4.5 million meant for the dairy farm, ended up here at Uxolo Diamond Cutting Works?

V/O: But the Asset Forfeiture Unit is trying to get the money back. All attempts to get comment from Uxolo were unsuccessful.

On the day they were paid R4.5 million, another R5 million was transferred to Islandsite Investments; R6 million to Annex Distribution, and R10 million to Oakbay Investments. A Director of all those companies is Gupta associate Ronica Ragavan. In total, the Asset Forfeiture Unit is claiming R68.5 million from companies she controls.

Devi: No, this isn’t a cowshed, these are the Oakbay offices in Sandton, where R24.5 million from the Vrede project, is being reclaimed under the Preservation Order as constituting the proceeds of crime. In court papers the NPA states that the entire Dairy Farm project was merely a scheme designed to defraud and steal monies from the department.

Devi: Do you believe the Guptas had any intention of fulfilling their mandate on the farm?

Pauli: It’s clear that they never had that intention. We didn’t know at the time that we were actually watching the guys who stole our eggs eating an omelette. It is terrible.

V/O: Estina didn’t even attempt to hide their Gupta connections, changing their registered address to 144 Katherine Street, Sandton – the same address as Oakbay. So, who is to blame?

Wayne: The Estina Dairy is a classic example of an individual at provincial government who has been moved because he influenced decisions at that level, to favour a family – a connected family – was moved then into the mining level at a ministerial level, to do the same thing.

V/O; OUTA, the Organization Undoing Tax Abuse, has laid charges of Treason against the former MEC of Agriculture, Mosebenzi Zwane, now Minister of Mineral Resources. CEO Wayne Duvenage explains.

Wayne: Treason at the highest level is, in a position of power that a minister like he is in, you need to act in the best interest of the country. You need to ensure that the decisions you make are not for self-enrichment or enrichment of individuals who shouldn't be enriched, but for the country. And he hasn't done that.

Devi: The Premier of the Free State, Ace Magashule, and the former MEC of Agriculture, Mosebenzi Zwane have both been regular visitors to Saxonwold. We asked both of them for comment on the Vrede Dairy farm project, but they don’t seem to be taking interviews.

V/O: However, Magashule is now the ANC Secretary-General, and spoke at a recent press conference about his family’s involvement with the Guptas.

Ace: My son has been working for the Guptas, it has never been a secret, and my son is not involved in the Vrede Dairy. Wherever there is corruption the law must take its place, whether it’s with Vrede Dairy or any other thing, the law must actually takes its place. So, let’s leave that matter, it’s with the NPA, with the law enforcers. Whatever happens we are reiterating the stance of the ANC: we need to fight corruption wherever it rears its head.

V/O: On Friday the Hawks raided the Free State Premier’s office, as well as the Department of Agriculture, in a search and seizure operation. Suddenly Carte Blanche received a reply from Magashule’s office stating that he “is not responsible for processing of payments or in supply chain processes, and cannot be linked to any alleged act of impropriety regarding this matter.”

Devi: January 2018, things seem to be moving faster?

Wayne: First of all, there’s this political will and there’s this moral courage to say corruption has to be dealt with. When you've got those 2 elements alone, political will and new leadership then things change fast and Cyril Ramaphosa has demonstrated that. So, we see all this new energy as a direct consequence of his election as the ANC president.

V/O: But what about the architects of this massive scam – the Guptas themselves?

Pauli: The moment that the Gupta Leaks were published, the Guptas would obviously have known okay we have problems here. And the first thing that you do is to move your assets, move your money out to keep it safe. You keep yourself safe, you keep your money safe and you keep your life safe.

V/O; South Africans thought they’d never see the fall of the Gupta empire, but this week has proved momentous.

Wayne: Chickens are coming home to roost, and fast! We’re in a very, very exciting phase. We are going to see some really interesting and good energy that tackles corruption in this country, that makes the investors sit up and that makes them take our new leadership seriously so that we can create jobs, we can get the national prosperity of this country to where it should be and ought to have been 9 years ago. Unfortunately, we've had a president who has captured the state and squandered billions and allowed us to go backwards as a nation. We have got a lot of nation building to do and this is an exciting period for us. We're excited.
